title: Non-Player-Controlled Nonterminal State
body_html:
Non-Player-Controlled Nonterminal State

A non-player-controlled state is a nonterminal state whose mover label is none. This is purely structural: it says that no strategic player controls the transition, but does not specify how the next action or successor is selected.

A probabilistic Nature/chance interpretation requires additional stochastic data and is tracked separately in [[game_theory.extensive_game.core.nature_player]].

References

  • [MFoGT, Section 6.2.5] Laraki, Renault, and Sorin, Mathematical Foundations of Game Theory. Nature nodes motivate distinguishing strategic control from non-player transitions; probability is additional data.

lean_refs.name: ControlledGame.isNonPlayerState
lean_refs.signature:
def isNonPlayerState (G : ControlledGame N) (s : G.State) : Prop :=
  G.mover s = none ∧ ¬ G.toArena.IsTerminal s
